               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Therefore whether <ns0:hi>it were</ns0:hi> I or they <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Whether I or any other of the Apostles preached amongst you.</ns0:note>, so we preached, and so ye believed <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This was one great point that we preached amongst you, That Christ was risen again from the dead. This we held forth to you as the object of your Faith, this you received and closed with as the object of your Faith; we did not only preach to you, That Christ <ns0:hi>died for our sins,</ns0:hi> but that he <ns0:hi>rose again for our Iustification.</ns0:hi> Neither was your Faith objected only in Christ, as one that was crucified, and had dyed, but as one that was risen from the dead. Thus <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> preached, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.31. & 3.15. & 4.20. & 5.30. and <ns0:hi>Stephen, Acts</ns0:hi> 7. and <ns0:hi>Peter, Acts</ns0:hi> 10.40. and <ns0:hi>Paul, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.37. & 18.3, 31. and so all the Apostles.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you, that there is no resurrection of the dead? <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Apostle having laid a good Foundation, proving the Resurrection of Christ by a plentiful Testimony of those who saw him after that he was risen from the dead; and minded them, That this was the Doctrine of the Gospel, which both they and all the rest of the Apostles, had with one consent preached to them; he comes to build upon it, and from this, as a main Argument to prove, That there must needs be a Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection from the dead; and beginneth with a reflection upon some in that Church who denied it: Who those were, we are not told; some think they were <ns0:hi>Hymeneus</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Philetus</ns0:hi> mentioned 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.17, 18. who held, that the Resurrection was past; others think, he reflects on <ns0:hi>Cerinthus,</ns0:hi> who was one of the Lea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of those Hereticks we read of, who after <ns0:hi>Simon Magus</ns0:hi> de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nied the Resurrection; others think, they were some of the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> of whom we read in the <ns0:hi>Acts,</ns0:hi> that they denied the <ns0:hi>Resurrection,</ns0:hi> or some of the <ns0:hi>Pharises,</ns0:hi> who denied the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of Christians,</ns0:hi> looking on them as <ns0:hi>Apostates</ns0:hi>; others think, they were some who had been tinctured at least with the Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Pagan Philosophers.</ns0:hi> We cannot certainly determine who, but certain it is, some there were; and the Apostle argues them in this thing to assert absurdly, upon this Supposition, That Christ was risen.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is not Christ risen <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>If</ns0:hi> (saith the Apostle) <ns0:hi>there be no Resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen</ns0:hi> But some will possibly say, How doth this follow? Suppose it true, that Christ be risen, how doth it follow, that the dead shall rise? The force of it lieth in several things. 1. Christ, as he saith, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. is the <ns0:hi>first-fruits of them that sleep,</ns0:hi> the exemplary cause of our Resurrection. 2. If we consider Christ as the <ns0:hi>Head,</ns0:hi> it is unreasonable, that the Head should be risen from the dead, and the Members yet held of Death, when it is the Office of the Head to communicate sense, life, and motion to the Members. Again, the Argument is strong from the consideration of the End of Christs Resurrecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, which was to shew his Victory over Death, that the dead might hear his Voice and live, and that he might be <ns0:hi>the Iudge of the quick and the dead,</ns0:hi> (which he could not have been, if the dead did not rise.) Now though it be true, that Christs Head<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship to his Church, and the Apostles Argument from thence will not prove the Resurrection of the wicked, yet (besides that the Resurrection of Believers is the main thing the Apostle here proveth, having elsewhere abundantly proved the general Resurrection) the consideration here of Christs being raised, that he might be the Judge both of the quick and of the dead, will prove the Resurrection of the wicked, as well as of Belie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And if Christ be not risen, then is our prea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ching vain <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Now (saith the Apostle) if Christ be not raised, in what a case are you? And we also, who have preached his Resurre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction to you? Our preaching is vain and false,</ns0:note>, and your faith is also vain <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">and your Faith is so also, for the object of it faileth, which is a Christ risen from the dead.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:456" />15 Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God, because we have testified of God, that he raised up Christ, whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">There is nothing in these two verses, but what the Apostle had before said, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That if Christ were not risen, the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles <ns0:hi>preaching,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Corinthians</ns0:hi> believing were both of them vain and false. Only what the Apostle, in the former verse, called Preaching, he here calleth <ns0:hi>Witnessing, We are</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>false witnesses of God.</ns0:hi> To be false Witnesses for men, or in the name of men, is against the ninth Commandment, and a sin of no ordinary magnitude; but to be a <ns0:hi>false Witness of God,</ns0:hi> is a much higher sin. This Title of <ns0:hi>Witnesses</ns0:hi> was at first given to the Apostles by Christ, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.8. afterwards often (especially in the <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi>) applied to them, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.22. & 2.32. & 4.33. & 5.32. & 10.39, 41. Particularly <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> applieth it to himself, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 22.15. & 26.16. It is true, the Apostles, who either saw Christ while he was on Earth after his Resurrection, or in Heaven, as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9. were in the strictest sense <ns0:hi>Eye-witnesses</ns0:hi>; but yet in a larger sense this notion agreeth to all Ministers, who testifie, upon the hearing of the Ears, and upon reading the Scriptures, the same thing which the Apostles testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fied, though not upon the same Evidence. Now to affirm a thing, as from God, for truth, which is in it self false, is a very high transgression: which (saith the Apostle) we must be guilty of, if Christ be not raised; and if the dead rise not, then Christ is not raised.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And if Christ be not raised, your faith <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> vain, ye are yet in your sins <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">That is, ye are yet in your estate of Nature, under the guilt and condemning power of your sins, which are not yet pardoned to you; for no sins are remitted, but upon believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, which none can do, if Christ be not risen from the dead; for by that he was <ns0:hi>declared to be the Son of God with power:</ns0:hi> his Death declared him to be truly Man, it was his Resurrection that manifested him to be truly God, God over all blessed for ever; and so the proper object of peoples Faith.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ, are perished <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Some think that the term <ns0:hi>in Christ</ns0:hi> in this Text, is of the same significancy with <ns0:hi>for the sake of Christ,</ns0:hi> which would re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strain it to <ns0:hi>Martyrs</ns0:hi>; but I know no reason for that, because what is said, it true of all; for it is plain, from what was said before, that if Christ be not risen from the dead, all that dye must dye in their fins, there being no object for their Faith to work or lay hold upon. The door of Salvation remaineth as fast shut as ever, so as those whom they looked upon as being asleep in Christ, must necessarily perish, if Christ be not risen; there is no <ns0:hi>Forerunner</ns0:hi> entred into the Heavens for us.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 If in this life onely we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Apostle here argueth the <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> of Believers from a new Head. It is not reasonable for any to imagine, that those who believe in Jesus Christ, should of all others be the most miserable; but this they must be, if there be no Resurrection from the dead. He inlargeth upon this Head of Argument fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 30, 31. The reason of it is, because it must then fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low, That they could have no hope in Christ beyond this life; and the condition of the <ns0:hi>Apostles,</ns0:hi> and the generality of Chri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stians, at least in those first and furious Times, was a most affli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cted state and condition. The Apostle was in Jeopardy every hour, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 30. he dyed daily, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. If any say, How doth this follow? for their Souls might be in Glory, though their bodies once dead, were not raised? It is answered: 1. That it still must hold as to their bodily, fleshly part. 2. That those who denied the Resurrection of the Body, denied also the Immor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tality of the Soul. 3. That <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> speaketh upon the supposition of the Divine Ordination; God having so ordered it, that the Death of Christ, without his Resurrection, should be of no a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vail to us to save either Soul or Body; and that our Souls and Bodies should not be separately, but joyntly glorified upon their re-union in the End of the World: 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.3. we are said to be <ns0:hi>begotten to a lively hope by the Resurrection of Iesus Christ from the dead.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 But now <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Pet. 1.3.</ns0:note> is Christ risen from the dead, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> become <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 26.23. Vers. 23. Rev. 1.5.</ns0:note> the first-fruits of them that sleep <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Apostle returneth to his former Argument, to dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course concerning the Resurrection of Christ, who is by him called the <ns0:hi>First-fruits of them that sleep</ns0:hi>; not of all that shall rise (as some think) for it will be hard to prove, That any benefit of Christs Death or Resurrection after this life, belongs to wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed men; nor is it usual for the Penmen of holy Writ, to ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />press the death of Unbelievers under the gentle notion of a sleep; and <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 1.18. Christ is called the <ns0:hi>First-born from the dead,</ns0:hi> as he is the <ns0:hi>Head of the Church.</ns0:hi> It is rather spoken with reference to Believers: the Resurrection of wicked men, flow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing rather from Gods Providence, in order to the manifestation of his Justice in the last Judgment, than from the Mediation of Christ. But here is a Question ariseth, How Christ is said to be the First-fruits of those that sleep, whenas we read of divers in Scripture, that were raised from the dead before Christ was so raised? <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> 1. Christ was the first that rose again by his own Power and Virtue. 2. He was the first who rose again, and died no more. 3. He was the first in respect of Dignity. 4. He was the First-fruits of them that sleep, by his Resurrecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on making a way for the Resurrection of others, even of all such as were Members of him; as the Offering of the First-fruits under the Law sanctified the whole Crop.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 5.12 17.</ns0:note> since by man <ns0:hi>came</ns0:hi> death <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Since by one man, <ns0:hi>viz. Adam,</ns0:hi> (who is also stiled the <ns0:hi>Son of God, Luke</ns0:hi> 3.28. because he had neither Father nor Mother) came mans subjection to mortality, sicknesses, and death here, and eternal death and misery in another World; it pleased God that by one, who though he was the Eternal only begotten Son of God, yet was also made Man, and was flesh of our flesh.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 11.29</ns0:note> by man <ns0:hi>came</ns0:hi> also the resurrection of the dead <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Resurrection of those that are Believers, and asleep in Christ, should come, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.14.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">As in the first <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> all men that were in him, became subject both to <ns0:hi>temporal death,</ns0:hi> and all the afflictions and miseries of this life, which are so many little deaths, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8. 36. and forerunners of natural death, or attendants upon it; and also to that <ns0:hi>eternal death</ns0:hi> which is the consequent of the guilt of sin, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.23. So in Christ, that is, through the Merits of his Death, and through his Resurrection, all that are in him, being chosen in him, given to him, and by Faith implanted into him, are not only spiritually made alive, (being passed from death to life, 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.14.) but shall be raised from the dead unto Eternal life. But though this Text doth not prove the general Resurre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction. (being only intended of Believers, that are Me<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ers of Christ) yet it doth not oppose it. But that the <ns0:hi>all</ns0:hi> here men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned is no more than <ns0:hi>all Believers,</ns0:hi> appeareth not only from the term <ns0:hi>in Christ</ns0:hi> in this verse, but from the whole fo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lowing Discourse; which is only concerning the Resurrection of Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers to life, not that of the wicked to eternal condemnation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But every man in his own order, Christ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Vers. 20.</ns0:note> the first-fruits <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>In his own order,</ns0:hi> either with respect to <ns0:hi>Time,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Dignity,</ns0:hi> lest any should say, If Christs Resurrection be the cause of the Resurrection of Believers, then why did not all the Saints, that were in the graves, rise with Christ? The Apostle sait<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, God had appointed an order, and this order was, that they th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> were dead, or should be dead, before Christs second Coming, should not prevent one another, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.15, &c. Besides, the order which God had set, was, That Christ should be the <ns0:hi>First-fruits</ns0:hi> of this Harvest, rising first from the dead, so as to dye no more.</ns0:note>, afterwards they that are Christs, at his coming <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Then Believers, that are Members of Christ by Faith implanted into him, should also rise, but not before his second Coming.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Then <ns0:hi>cometh</ns0:hi> the end <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The End of all the miseries and afflictions, which Believers meet with in this life, or the End of all our Preaching and Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistry, the End of the World, or the End of Man, or rather (as the next words seem to interpret it) the End of that me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diatory Kingdom of Christ, which he now administreth instead of his Father, and shall manage to the End of the World.</ns0:note>, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Christ shall then deliver up those Keys of Life, and Hell, and Death to his Father, yet shall not Christs Kingdom cease, (for the Prophet saith, <ns0:hi>That of it there shall be no end:</ns0:hi>) Christs es<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sential Kingdom, which is his Dominion, which he hath, and exerciseth over all created Beings, together with his Father, and the holy Spirit, (all being but one Divine Essence) that shall hold and abide for ever; but his mediatory Kingdom, by which he ruleth over his Church in the midst of his Enemies, that shall cease, and be delivered up unto the Father: So that Christs delivering up the Kingdom to his Father, proveth no inferiority of Christ to his Father, more than his Fathers com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mitting that mediatory Kingdom to him can prove his Fathers not reigning, or inferiority to him, which it certainly doth not. It signifieth only the ceasing of that Disp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tion, or Christs exercise of his mediatory Kingdom on Earth, in the Rule and Government of the Church, and subduing his and his Peoples Enemies.</ns0:note>, when he shall have put down all rule, and all authority, and power <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Then shall all Rule and Authority of Kings and Princes of the Earth cease, and all the ministration of good Angels, and power of evil Angels; so shall all Ministra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions and Governments in the Church Militant here on Earth, and all those that are the Enemies of the Church shall be subdu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed and brought under.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:456" />25 For he must reign, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>cts 2.34. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1.13. & <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.13.</ns0:note> until he hath put all enemies under his feet <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">God hath so decreed, (and what he hath said must come to pass) that Christ should, as Mediator, exercise a Kingdom and Government in the World, until he hath subdued all the Enemies of his Gospel and People; all those who have said, <ns0:hi>He shall not rule over them</ns0:hi>; the whole World that lieth in wicked<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, the Devil, and all his Instruments: this he proveth from the words of the Psalmist, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110.2. The term <ns0:hi>until</ns0:hi> doth not signifie the determination of Christs Kingdom then, though his mediatory Kingdom on Earth will then be determined. He shall still reign, but not as now, in the midst of his Enemies, and in the exercise of his Kingdom in the Conquest and subdu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 20.14.</ns0:note> The last enemy <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> shall be destroyed, <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> death <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">If <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi> be an Enemy (as we usually judge) that also must be destroyed; and there is no other way to destroy Death, but by the causing of a Resurrection from the dead. So that the Apostle proveth the Resurrection from the necessity of Christs reigning, until all his Enemies be destroyed, of which Death is one; for it keeps the bodies of the Members of Christ from their Union with their Souls, and with Christ, who is the Head of the whole Believer, the Body as well as the Soul.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 28.18.</ns0:note> For he hath put all things under this feet <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The Apostle referreth to <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 8.6. where the <ns0:hi>Psalmist</ns0:hi> adoreth God for the Priviledges given man in his Creation; a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst which this is one, That God had put all things under his feet; the <ns0:hi>Psalmist</ns0:hi> afterward expounds that universal Particle, v. 7, 8. by <ns0:hi>All Sheep</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Oxen,</ns0:hi> yea and <ns0:hi>the beasts of the field,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>sowls of the Air, and the fishes of the Sea.</ns0:hi> But that that Psalm, or some passages at least in it, are to be understood of Christ, appeareth from <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.6, 7, 8. where the Penman applieth it to him, as doth the Apostle here; under whose feet all things are put in a much larger sense, and therefore the Apostle expounds the Affirmative, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.8. by a Negative, <ns0:hi>He left nothing that is not put under him.</ns0:hi> But left men of perverse minds should conclude, That then the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> also <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s <ns0:hi>put under Christ,</ns0:hi> the Apostle addeth; That</ns0:note>; But when he saith all things are put under <ns0:hi>him, it is</ns0:hi> manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">when he saith, <ns0:hi>He hath put all things under his feet,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> himself, who is the Person that put all things under him, is not to be included.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And when all things shall be subdued unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 3.23. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 11.3.</ns0:note> then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The Sons subjection to his Father, which is mentioned in this place, doth no where prove his inequality of Essence, or Power with his Father; it only signifieth what was spoken be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, that Christ should deliver up his <ns0:hi>Mediatory Kingdom</ns0:hi> to his Father; so manifesting, that whatsoever he had done in the Office of Mediator, was done in the Name of his Father, and by his Power and Authority, and that as he was Man, he was subject to his Father. Suppose (saith <ns0:hi>Pareus</ns0:hi>) a King should have one only Son, whom he should take into a Partnership with him in his <ns0:hi>Majesty</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi>; but yet so, that the <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> should still have the Preheminence of a Father, the Son only the Dignity of a Son in such Power and Authority; after which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> King having some Subjects risen up in Rebellion against him, should send his Son with Armies and his Authority against them, he would dispatch the work, and at his return yield up his Commission to his Father, yet still retaining the same Nature he had, and Authority with which his Father had before cloath<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, as a Partner in the Kingdom and Government with him.</ns0:note>, that God may be all in all <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">That God (saith the Apostle) may be <ns0:hi>all in all.</ns0:hi> Instead of all <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which the heart of man can wish; or that God may <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in full and perfect Empire and Government over all things; That the incomprehensible Glory of God may fill all the Elect. But is not God in this World all in all? <ns0:hi>Answ. He is</ns0:hi>; but he doth not so appear ruling in the midst of his Enemies here. 2. The Government will be alter'd; God here is sole King of the World, but he partly ruleth in by Christ, as Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or, whose mediatory Kingdom shall then cease, and nothing shall<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> appear but the essential Kingdom of God; the Power by which the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, (three Persons, though but one God) shall govern and rule all things, when all this sublunary World shall cease.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead. If the dead rise not all, why are they then baptized for the dead? <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">A very difficult Text, and variously expounded. The terms <ns0:hi>Baptize</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Baptism</ns0:hi> signifie no more in their original and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signification, than <ns0:hi>to wash,</ns0:hi> and a Washing. The <ns0:hi>wash<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of Pots</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cups</ns0:hi> in use amongst the Jews, is in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> The <ns0:hi>Baptisms</ns0:hi> of Pots and Cups; but the most usual acception of i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in Scripture, is to sig<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>fie one of the Sacraments of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Test<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that Sacred action, by which one is washed according to the Institution of Christ, <ns0:hi>In the Name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> It is also Metaphorically used by our Saviour in the Gospels, <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 20.22, 23. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 10.39. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 12.50. to signifie a Suffering for the Name of Christ. And it is also used thus <ns0:hi>Metaphorically,</ns0:hi> to signifie the Action of the Holy Ghost in cleansing and renewing our hearts, <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 3. 11, 12. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.5. The last usage of the term is by no means applicable here. The Question is, Whether the Apostle mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth here only, Why are <ns0:hi>men washed for the dead?</ns0:hi> Or why are men <ns0:hi>baptized</ns0:hi> religiously for the dead? Or why are <ns0:hi>men baptized with blood for the dead?</ns0:hi> For the <ns0:hi>Popish</ns0:hi> Notion, That Baptism here signifies any <ns0:hi>Religious Actions,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Fastings,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prayers,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Penances</ns0:hi> for those that are in <ns0:hi>Purgatory,</ns0:hi> there is no such usage of the term in Scripture; for though in Scripture it signifies sometimes Sufferings from the hands of others, as in <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 20.22, 23. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 10.39. yet it no where signifies Penances, or such Sufferings as men impose upon themselves for the dead. Nor doth <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> here say, To what purpose <ns0:hi>do men baptize them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves,</ns0:hi> but why are they baptized for the dead? 1. Those that think the term here signifies washing, <ns0:hi>what shall they do, who are washed for the dead?</ns0:hi> tell us, That it being a custom in many Countries, for neatness and cleanliness, to wash dead bodies: the Primitive Christians used that Ceremony as a <ns0:hi>Religious Rite,</ns0:hi> and a testification of their Belief of the Resurrection. That such a custom was in use amongst Christians, is plain from <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9.37. but that they used it as a <ns0:hi>Religious Rite,</ns0:hi> or a testimony of their Faith in the Resurrection, appeareth not. And though it be <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, yet they say <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is so used, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.8. <ns0:hi>for the Truth of God,</ns0:hi> expounded by the next word, <ns0:hi>to confirm the Promises.</ns0:hi> 2. Those that think, that by <ns0:hi>baptizing</ns0:hi> in this Text, the <ns0:hi>Sacra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of Baptism</ns0:hi> is to be understood, give us more than one ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count. 1. Some say, That whereas they were wont in the Primitive Church, before they admitted persons into a full Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />munion with the Church, to keep them for some time under Catechism, in which time they were called <ns0:hi>Catechumeni</ns0:hi>; if such sell sick, and in danger of death, <ns0:hi>they baptized them</ns0:hi>; or if they dyed suddenly, they baptized some other for them, in testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony of their hope of the joyful Resurrection of such a person to Eternal life. Now admit this were an errour of practice in them, as to this Ordinance; yet if any such thing were in pra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctice in this Church, the Argument of the Apostle was good a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst them. But how shall any such thing be made appear to us, That there was such an early corruption in this Church? Others say, That some believing the Resurrection, would upon their death-beds be baptized, in testimony of it, from whence they had the Name of <ns0:hi>Clinici.</ns0:hi> Others say, To be <ns0:hi>baptized for the dead</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> signifieth to be baptized when they were dying, and so as good as dead. Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> chuseth this sense; but the Que<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stion is, Whether the Greek Phrase <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> will bear it. Others tell us of a custom in use in the Primitive Church, to baptize persons over the Graves of the Martyrs, as a testimony of their Belief of the Resurrection. That there was anciently such a custom, I doubt not: And I believe that the custom with us in reading of Prayers over dead Bodies at the Grave, doth much more probably derive from this ancient-usage, than the Papists praying for the dead; but that there was any such custom so ancient as the Apostles times, I very much doubt. There are yet two other senses given of this difficulty Phrase, ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther of which seemeth to me much more probable than any of these. To the first we are led by the next verse, <ns0:hi>Or why are we in jeopardy every hour?</ns0:hi> Which inclineth many good Interpre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters to think, that the Baptism here mentioned i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. That <ns0:hi>Baptism with Blood</ns0:hi> mentioned by our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>0<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 22, 23 and so the sense is no more, than if there be no Resurrection of the dead, why do we dye daily? Why are we killed all the day long? For we do that in hope of a blessed Resurrection. The only Objections against this are, 1. That none but Christ him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self useth the word in this sense, (which seemeth a light exce<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ption.) 2. That <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is hardly capable of that sense; but yet our Learned Dr. <ns0:hi>Lightfoot</ns0:hi> brings parallels of such an usage of the Preposition out of the LXX. Others observe, that the Apostle, in this whole Chapter, is discoursing of the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of Believers unto life,</ns0:hi> and they are such dead alone, that he here speaketh of, for whom he saith any were baptized. Now it is plain from Scripture, that Baptism is a Seal of the Resurrection, signifying to Believers, that they shall be made partakers of the Death and Resurrection of Christ, (the Resurrection being strongly proved from Gods Covenant, of which Baptism is a Seal, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 20.37, 38:) and being so, it confirmed the Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant, not only to the persons baptized, but to the whole Church, as well the Triumphant as the Militant part of it; as well with reference to those of it that were dead, as those that were li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving. So that so often as Baptism was administred in the Church, so often God repeated the Covenant made to his whole Church, that he was the God of Believers and of their Seed: So that all who to this day are baptized, are baptized for the dead, that is, for the confirmation of Gods Covenant to his whole Church, as well that part of it which is dead, as that part which is yet alive; and it testifieth, that those that sleep in Christ (although dead) yet live in the promise of the Resurrection, because God is their God, and he is not the God of the dead, but of the li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving, as our Saviour speaketh in <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 20.38. In this variety a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst Learned men about the true sense of this place, I shall leave the Reader to his own judgment; although to me the two last seem to be most probable.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:457" />30 And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">We are the veriest Fools in Nature, if there be no Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />surrection of Believers unto Life; for it is in the firm belief and hopes of that, that we are in danger of our lives, and all that we have, every hour of our lives.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 I protest by <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Some read our.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thess. 2.19.</ns0:note> your rejoycing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 8.36. Chap. 4.9. 2 Cor. 4.10, 11.</ns0:note> I die daily <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">What is meant here by <ns0:hi>your rejoycing which I have,</ns0:hi> is some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing doubted; some understanding it of the Apostles rejoycing in them as Believers, whom he had been an Instrument to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vert, and bring home to Christ: others of their <ns0:hi>rejoycing in him</ns0:hi> (which seems not probable, many of them so much despi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing and vilifying him:) others understand it, of their glory<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing against him, and triumphing over him, and that this was one of his sufferings which he instanceth in, which he under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />went in hope of a Ressurection. The words are not an Oath, (for here God is not called to witness) they are only an <ns0:hi>Attesta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi> As the Prophets sometimes call Heaven and Earth to wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, so here he calls their <ns0:hi>Rejoycing</ns0:hi> to witness; and this re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joycing seems to be the joy of those who amongst them truly rejoyced in Jesus Christ, for which also he rejoyced daily, they being the Seal of his Apostleship. That which he solemnly affirms, is, That <ns0:hi>he died daily</ns0:hi>; not only was ready to dye dai<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, but in the same sense that he elsewhere saith, he was in <ns0:hi>Deaths often,</ns0:hi> and that they were <ns0:hi>killed all the day long</ns0:hi>; suffer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing such afflictions as were near a kin to death, and led on to death, as their end.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 If <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>to speak after the man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner of men.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 22.13. & 56.12.</ns0:note> Let us eat and drink, for to morrow we shall die <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Concerning this Fight of the Apostle with <ns0:hi>Beasts at Ephesus,</ns0:hi> there are two Opinions; some thinking that he indeed fought with Beasts, and we know that in those Countries such a pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment was in use, to bring out Malesectors to fight with wild Beasts; but as we read in the <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> of no such dealings with <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> so that being a punishment rather for their slaves and vilest men, it can hardly be thought that <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> who was a Free-man of <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> should be exposed to it: They seem therefore better to understand it, who interpret it of his conflict with men, who in their conditions and manners were like beasts; and that he doth not speak here of his scuffle with <ns0:hi>Demetrius,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19. but some other conflict he had there, of which the Scripture giveth us no large account, but it seems to be gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally and obscurely mentioned in the next Epistle, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.8. for this Epistle was wrote after his contest with <ns0:hi>Demetrius.</ns0:hi> By that Phrase, <ns0:hi>after the manner of men,</ns0:hi> some think he means, as men use to fight; some have other notions of it: the sense seems to be plainly this, If I have fought with beastly men at <ns0:hi>Ephesus</ns0:hi> after the manner that men fight with beasts, exposing my body to their rage and fury, what profit is it to me, if the dead rise not? I have opposed my self to their fury out of an hope for a joyful Resurrection; but if there shall be no such Resurrection, the <ns0:hi>Epicures</ns0:hi> that resolve to stick at nothing, nor to deny themselves in any sensual satisfaction from meat and drink, have the best of it; all men had then best sing their Song, <ns0:hi>Let us eat and drink,</ns0:hi> for we have but a little time to eat and to drink in<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> we know that we shall dye, and there will be an end of us.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Be not deceived: evil communications cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt good manners <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Do not suffer your selves to be abused with evil and corrupt discourses of those Philosophers amongst whom you converse, who argue from innate Principles of Reason against Articles of Faith; though you may judge, that they talk but for discourse sake, yet their communication or discourse is naught, and will influence men as to things of practice, and debauch men in their Morals. It is a Verse or Saying taken out of, or at least found in, one of the Pagan Poets; but containing in it much truth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Awake to righteousness, and sin not <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Sin is in Scripture compared, to <ns0:hi>sleep, Rom.</ns0:hi> 13.11. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.14. and that very properly; for as the natural Senses are bound up in natural sleep, so the Sinners spiritual Senses are locked up, so that he doth not exercise them to discern betwixt good and evil; and as he that is asleep, is void of all care and fear, is secure, so the Sinner is secure and void of fear. And Repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance is set out under the notion of <ns0:hi>awaking</ns0:hi>; we are not only concerned to eschew evil, but to do good; not only to awake from Sin, but to <ns0:hi>Righteousness,</ns0:hi> that is, to an holy life and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versation, that is it which is here called Righteousness, all spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual rectitude being to be judged from the Souls conformity to the Divine Rule; hence sin is called a crooked way, because it will not agree with the Rule of Gods Word.</ns0:note>: for some have not the knowledge of God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">For some a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst you have not a due and saving Knowledge of God, or a right apprehension of the things of God,</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.5.</ns0:note> I speak this to your shame <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">though it be a shame for them that have it not, considering the light and means of knowledge which you have had by my Ministry, and the Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistry of others who have been amongst you.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 But some man will say, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 37.3.</ns0:note> How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come? <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Some of your vain Philosophers, who are resolved to give credit to nothing upon the account of a bare Divine Revelation, unless they can give a farther rational account of it in the cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumstances, will be ready to object and say, How is it possible, that those very bodies which are putrefied, and turned into dust, and that dust, it may be, scattered to the four Winds, should be raised up? And if the same bodies shall not again rise, what kind of bodies shall the Believers have in the Resurrection? Shall they be bodies that will need meat, and drink, and cloaths, as our present bodies do? Or what other bodies shall they be?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Thou fool <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">He saith not, <ns0:hi>thou fool</ns0:hi> in anger, (which is that using of this term which our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 5.22. saith, brings a man under the gift of Hell fire) but in the way of a grave and authoritative reproof; calling them Fools for their want of a due understand<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the things and ways of God.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 12.24.</ns0:note> that which thou sowest is not quickned, except it die <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He lets them know, that they might as well ask, how the grain of Wheat, which they ordinarily sowed in their field, did rise again? For that grain al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so rotteth under the clods of the earth, under which it is buried, before it again riseth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or some other <ns0:hi>grain</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And when it again riseth, or shooteth up, it is not bare grain, without either stalk or ear, (which was the body by them sown.)</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 But God giveth it a body as it pleaseth him, and to every seed its own body <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But God giveth to every grain, or kind of seed, such a kind of body as it pleased him, and a several body, according to the nature of the grain; yet none will deny, but it is the seed sown which cometh up, though with a different body, in respect of some qualities.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 All shesh <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not the same flesh, but <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> one <ns0:hi>kind</ns0:hi> of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> another of birds <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Flesh is a kind of body, but it is of various degrees of dig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity and excellency, in respect of the qualities of it: the flesh of men is of a differing excellency from the flesh of beasts; and there is a difference in natural Qualities betwixt the corporeal Substances of Beasts, and of Fishes, and Birds; yet they a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e all bodies, they are all flesh; our disti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ction betwixt <ns0:hi>Flesh</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fish,</ns0:hi> it is but according to our Idiom or propriety of speaking we read of the <ns0:hi>fl<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sh</ns0:hi> of fish, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 11.10, 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 <ns0:hi>There are</ns0:hi> also celestial bodies <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Such are the Sun, the Moon, and the Stars.</ns0:note>, and bodies terrestrial <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Men, Beasts, Birds, Fishes, the Elements, Stones, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: But the glory of the celestial <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> one, and the <ns0:hi>glory</ns0:hi> of the terrestrial <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> another <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Now betwixt these two Species of Bodies, in respect of Qualities, there is a very great difference; the glory of the heavenly Bodies is much greater than the glory of the earthy Bodies that are compound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed of the Elements.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> star differeth from <ns0:hi>another</ns0:hi> star in glory <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Amongst the celestial Bodies, there is a great deal of diffe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence with respect to the Qualities; one of them is in glory much differing from another, the glory of the Moon is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ot like the glory of the Sun, and the glory of a Star is much beneath the glory both of the Sun and of the Moon; yea, one Star is more glorious than another, yet they are all Bodies, though of different Species and Qualities.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Dan. 12. Matt. 13.4</ns0:note> So also <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the resurrection of the dead <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">That is, so shall it be, as to the bodies of the Saints, in the Resurrection. The same bodies of the Saints shall rise, though with qualities, and in a condition much different from what they were when they fell; as the same grain of Wheat shooteth up, though with another body; and as there is a diffe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence betwixt celestial and terrestrial Bodies, and betwixt cele<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stial Bodies themselves: so there will be a difference betwixt the bodies of the Saints, now that they are only of the Earth earthly, from what they shall be in the Resurrection; which difference he openeth in several particulars.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Phil. 3.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> it is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ption <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>It is sown,</ns0:hi> that is, it dyeth, and is buried in such a state, that it is subject to putre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />faction; but when it shall be again raised from the dead, it shall be subject to no putrefaction or corruption: So <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 52. <ns0:hi>The dead shall be raised incorruptible.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 It is sown in dishonour, it is raised in glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">There is nothing more uncomely, unlovely, and loathsom than a dead body; but it will not be so when it shall be raised again, then it shall be a <ns0:hi>beautiful,</ns0:hi> comely body. We shall rise in a full and perfect age, (as is generally thought) and without those defects and deformities, which may here make our bodies appear unlovely. <ns0:hi>Daniel, Chap.</ns0:hi> 12.2. says, <ns0:hi>The righteous shall shine as the Stars:</ns0:hi> Christ saith, <ns0:hi>They shall shine like the Sun:</ns0:hi> the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.21. <ns0:hi>we shall be made like unto his glorious Body.</ns0:hi> Three things make the body beautiful, a perfection of parts, the well putting them together, and proportioning them one to another, and a well tempered chearly spirit; all these will concur in the bodies of Saints in the Resurrection. The Shoolmen determine, That much of the beauty of the Saints bodies in the Resurrection, will flow from their perfect sight of God, and the reflection of God upon them.</ns0:note>: it is sown in weakness, it is raised in pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">When it dyeth, it is a frail weak body, unable to resist injuries, but it shall rise a strong body, with quick senses, and subject to no more weak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:457" />44 It is sown a natural body <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Such a body as all living Creatures have by Nature, which is upheld by the actions of the Soul that quickeneth it, both the <ns0:hi>Vegetative</ns0:hi> powers, by which it is nourished by the use of meat and drink, the eating, concocting, and digesting it, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and the sensitive powers, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, it is raised a spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritual body <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">But it shall be raised a <ns0:hi>spiritual Body.</ns0:hi> Spiritual, not as to the substance of it, (for in that sense a <ns0:hi>spiritual Body</ns0:hi> is a contradiction;) but in respect of the qua<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lities and conditions of it, <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 22.30. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 20.35, 36. Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies, which, in respect of many new qualities they shall have, shall be more like <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> and other <ns0:hi>Spirits,</ns0:hi> than humane bodies. Beautiful, incorruptible, free from infirmities, not subject to hunger, or thirst, or iniuries, from cold or heat, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> not using meat, drink, cloaths, physick, or marriage: Free, active, and nimble as Spirits, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.17. <ns0:hi>Spiritual,</ns0:hi> because they shall perfectly obey the Soul made perfect, and be by it commanded to spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual actions only; of <ns0:hi>subtile, spiritual, refined Constitutions.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 And so it is written: The first man Adam was made a living soul <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The first part is written in <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 2.7. God <ns0:hi>breathed into mans nostrils the breath of life, and so he became a living Soul</ns0:hi>; that is, a living substance, living an animal, natural life, by virtue of that breath of life, which God breathed into him.</ns0:note>, the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 5.14.</ns0:note> last Adam <ns0:hi>was made</ns0:hi> a quickening Spirit <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The last <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> by which he meaneth Christ, who in time was after the first <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> and was born in the last days, and was the last com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon Head; as <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> was the first, with respect of natural and carnal propagation, so Christ was the last Head, in repect of Grace and spiritual Regeneration, he was made a <ns0:hi>quickening Spirit.</ns0:hi> He was <ns0:hi>made</ns0:hi> so, not when he was conceived and born, for he had a Body subject to the same <ns0:hi>natural infirmities</ns0:hi> that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> are; but upon his <ns0:hi>Resurrection from the dead,</ns0:hi> when, though he had the same Body, in respect of the substance of it, yet it differed in qualities, and was much more spiritual; with which Body he ascended up into Heaven, cloathed with a Power as to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>cken Souls with a spiritual life, so also to quicken our mortal bodies at his second Coming, when he shall raise the <ns0:hi>dead</ns0:hi> out of their Graves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Howbeit that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural, and afterwards that which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> spritual <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Christ, the spiritual <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> was not first in order of time, but the natural <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi>; God in his Providence rising from more imperfect to more perfect Dispensations: and so it is as to Gods Providences relating unto us, we have first natural bodies, we are born with such, we grow up and dye with such, but then we shall rise again with others, in respect of excellenter quali<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties and endowments.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 The first man <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> of the earth, earthy: the second man <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the Lord <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> from heaven <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> who was the first Man, was of the Earth, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.7. and was of an earthy constitution, like unto the Earth out of which he was formed; but Christ had another Original: For though his Body was formed in the Womb of the Virgin, and he was flesh of her flesh, yet she conceived by the Holy Ghost over shadowing her, and Christ had an eternal Generation (us to his Divine Nature) from his Father.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 As <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the earthy, such <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they also that are earthy: and as <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the heavenly, such <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they also that are heavenly <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Such a body as <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> had, (which was earthly) such all the Sons of <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> have; and such a Body as Christ now hath since his Resurrection, (which is an heavenly Body) such a bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy also shall Believers, who are heavenly, have in the Resurre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 5.3. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Cor. 3.18. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.11. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 3.21.</ns0:note> as we have born the image of the earthy, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 3.1.</ns0:note> we shall also bear the image of the hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venly <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">And as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lievers, being the natural Sons of the first <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> have <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>orn his Image, had such bodies as he had while they li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved here; so they shall also in the Resurrection bear the Image of the heavenly, the Image of Christ; that is, have such bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies as was Christs Body, after that he was again risen from the dead.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 Now this I say, brethren, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 3.3.5.</ns0:note> flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Flesh and blood do not here signifie Sin, the unrenewed Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, (as some would have it) but <ns0:hi>our bodies,</ns0:hi> in their present natural, corruptible, frail, mortal state; so the terms signifie, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.14. <ns0:hi>Flesh</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Blood</ns0:hi> shall inherit the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of God, (else our bodies could not be glorified) but our body, as in its present state, till changed and altered, as to quali<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties, till it be made as spiritual body, shall not inherit the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of God.</ns0:note>, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther doth corruption inherit incorruption <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The latter words give a reason, why flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, because it is <ns0:hi>Cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruption,</ns0:hi> that is, subject to natural corruption and pu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>refaction, and the heavenly state is a sta<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e of incorruption; the bodies of Believers therefore must be raised up in that state of incorrup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42. before they can be capable of inheriting the Kingdom of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 Behold, I shew you a mystery <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">They might object, How can this be? There will be ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny Saints alive in the World at the day, when Christ shall come to judge the World, they will have natural bodies, such as they were born with, and grew up with in the World until that time (saith the Apostle) I now tell you a secret thing, (for so the term <ns0:hi>Mystery</ns0:hi> signifieth, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.25. & 16.25. and in many other Texts.)</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thess. 4.15, 16, 17.</ns0:note> We shall not all sleep <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">We shall not all sleep any long sleep: Some think all shall dye, but some for a very short time, and then they shall revive.</ns0:note>, but we shall all be changed <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">But we shall <ns0:hi>all be changed,</ns0:hi> either dying for a time, or by some other work of God their natural, corruptible bodies shall be turned into spiritual bodies, not capable of cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruption.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">This Change will be on the sudden, in a moment; either upon the Will and Command of Christ, which shall be as effe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctual to call persons out of their Graves, as a Trumphet is to call persons together; or rather, upon a Sound made like to the Sound of a Trumpet; as it was at the giving of the Law upon <ns0:hi>Sinai, Exod.</ns0:hi> 19.16. We read of this last <ns0:hi>Trump, Matt.</ns0:hi> 24.31. 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.16 There shall (saith the Apostle) be such a Sound made, and upon the making of it, the Saints, that are dead, shall be raised out of their Graves; not with such bodies as they carried thither, (which were corruptible) but with such bodies as shall be no more subject to corruption; and those who at that time shall be alive, shall one way or another be <ns0:hi>changed,</ns0:hi> and be also put into an incorruptible state.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 For this corruptible must put on incorrupti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 5.4.</ns0:note> and this mortal <ns0:hi>must</ns0:hi> put on immortality <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">God hath so deceed, That our flesh and blood<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in the state wherein now it is, shall not be glorified; it shall be the same body as to the substance, but not as to the qualities; it is now corruptible and mortal, it must be put into a state of in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />corruption and immortality, before it can enter into the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of Heaven.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That is, in an eternal and continuing Victory; the Saints shall dye no more The quotation which the Apostle bringeth, is out of those two Texts, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 25.8. <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 13.14. which two Texts the Apostle saith, at that day will have a more full, per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect, and eminent accomplishment, than ever they before had.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Hos. 13.14.</ns0:note> O death, where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thy sting <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The Apostle, in the contemplation of this blessed day, tri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />umpheth over death; in a Metaphorical Phrase, <ns0:hi>Where is thy sting?</ns0:hi> What hurt canst thou now do unto Believers, more than a Wasp, or Hornet, or Bee, that hath lost its sting?</ns0:note>? O <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>O Hell.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> grave, where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thy victory? <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">O <ns0:hi>Grave,</ns0:hi> or O <ns0:hi>Hell,</ns0:hi> (the same word signifieth both) where now is thy Victory? The Conquerour of all flesh is now conquered, the Spoiler of all men is spoiled; it had got a Victory, but now, O Death, where is thy Victory?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="56">56 The sting of death <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> sin <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">If it were not for sin, death could have no power over man; Sin is that which giveth death a power to hurt the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of men; <ns0:hi>the wages of sin is death, Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.23.</ns0:note>, and the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 5.13. & 7.5.13.</ns0:note> strength of sin <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the Law <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">And without the Law there could be no transgression. The Law is so far from taking away the guilt of sin, that through the corruption of our Natures, strongly inclining us to what is forbidden, it addeth strength to sin; <ns0:hi>Sin</ns0:hi> (as the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 7.8.) <ns0:hi>taking occasion by the commandment, and working in us all man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner of concupiscence.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="57">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:458" />57 But thanks <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> to God, which giveth us <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Joh. 5.5.</ns0:note> the victory, through our Lord Jesus Christ <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The Victory over Sin and over Death, we have both through the Death and the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ; who by his Death both delivered us from the guilt of sin, and also from the power of sin; and who through death destroyed him who had the power of death, even the Devil.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye sted<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Apostle concludeth his Discourse, proving the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection of the Body from the dead, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ounding upon it an Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hortation to Holiness; which is here called <ns0:hi>the work of the Lord,</ns0:hi> because it is made up of works done by us at the command of Christ, and with a direct respect to his Glory in obedience to his Will. He mindeth them not only to do these things, but to do them <ns0:hi>stedfastly</ns0:hi>; not by fits, but never turning aside from them either one way or another; and <ns0:hi>unmoveably,</ns0:hi> so as no tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ptations either from dangers, or rewards, or false Teachers, should shake their Faith, as to the Principles, that lead unto such an holy life; this especially of the Resurrection from the dead.</ns0:note>, for as much as ye know that your la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour is not in vain in the Lord <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Because they knew, that through the Grace of God, and the Merits of Christ, such works as these should not want their re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward; for though the work of God be wages to it self, and Christians should not serve God <ns0:hi>meerly</ns0:hi> for wages, yet it is law<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful for them (as for <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>) to have an eye to the Recompence of Reward; and a greater reward than this of the Resurrection of the Body to Eternal life, and that in a state of <ns0:hi>immortality</ns0:hi> and incorruption, in a spiritual and honourable estate, could not be.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
